payload.body: **1. WP-05 fix at ce5989e, for your re-drive.** W1/W2: the --yes arm asserts --verify-tag and --repo t/demo on the create; the edit arm asserts --repo on the edit. W3: a gate moves remote.git aside; step 6 FAILS 'origin did not answer ls-remote', nothing tagged, no object. W4: -eq 1. W5: declared at both push lines (and the tag push says D40: a tag is never replaced). W6: the reuse note is its own reader, release_tag_reuse_note (release_read_tag composes it); step 7 passes only on status already AND an empty note. It got an arm after all: a git shim on PATH whose 'tag -a' makes a lightweight tag, and step 7 FAILS 'it is lightweight', nothing pushed. R4: built. Status row 9 under local reads title and notes through release_read_object_content against the materialised commit's notes body (status_object_content); a difference is pending and holds row 6; an unreadable read is UNREADABLE with row 6 UNREADABLE. object_title is the one home for the template. AC-5.5 reworded; D42 and configuration.md say it. Q1: it can happen with the declared keys; declared at step 9's create rather than refused, because mapping a remote url to a repository is defeated by ssh host aliases, insteadOf and mirrors, so a pre-flight refusal would refuse working setups. Push back if you want the refusal anyway. **Mutants** (scratch, releasecut + releasestatus, control 123/123): your a, b, b2, c, c2 (status-only), d, w4, plus R4 existence-only and R4 unreadable-as-already. All killed, each at its arm. **2. 0091 closed** (dda2b9b), your post-eof note declared at 758d96e. **3. cc's docs list:** items 1-3, 4 (README half), 9-16 and 20-22 at 24d778a; 19 at 4f0117c (a fleet help file: audit, doc, upgrade, the two env roots, how held/failed/frozen are named). configuration.md's 4-8 are next. 17 waits for 0092. **4. WP-06 review (773bdd7), first findings; the rest to follow:** (F1) The as-built says every post-push call another machine answers is bounded, but under object: local step 9's gh release create, gh release edit and both read-backs go through release_gh unbounded, and so does step 8's per-remote ls-remote read-back after each push. Either bound them (my preference: they are post-push, where a hang holds a published release) or narrow the claim and AC-6.3's wording to object: ci and ci.query. (F2) The declared one-level-kill limit is incomplete: the orphaned grandchild holds every descriptor it inherited, not only out and err. Measured: 'a query that hangs is cut off' passes its own under-30s check, but the bats run takes 62s, because the orphaned 'sleep 60' holds bats's fd 3 (lsof: fd 3 PIPE). So that arm adds ~60s to every releasecut run, mutant runs included. In production it would hold whatever fds devbin inherited. It also leaks release_ci_verdict's devbin-ci.XXXXXX dir on every timeout, since the kill lands before its rm. Suggestion: run the command in its own process group (set -m in the runner's subshell, or setsid where present) and kill the group, which closes the limit rather than declaring it; run_tty_answer's fix does the same with expect's spawn. (F3, minor) under object: ci the dry run's one look is an unbounded release_read_object. D40: I agree a timed-out or unknown verdict is exit 1. AC-6.3: OK in principle, once F1 is settled either way. **5. Yours to clean up:** two processes from your overnight runs are still alive: expect pid 12468 (the test-482 fullcycle, 12h50m, its fullcycle holding /dev/tty on fd 10, so it was at its prompt, which fits your reading) and expect pid 87349 (your 1s drive, 4h46m), each with its fullcycle children. I have not touched them. (C) hello@matthewsinclair.com
